title: Media Coverage and Protection of Identity for Persons Undergoing Trials for Sex Crimes
what_it_is: Media Coverage and Protection of Identity for Persons Undergoing Trials for Sex Crimes

sections.label: Anonymity for accused persons abroad
sections.summary: The first approach favours protecting accused persons' identity until conviction, with examples from Ireland, Switzerland, New Zealand and Australia.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Law (Mr K Shanmugam)
sentences.text: The first approach leans in favour of protecting the identity of accused persons if and until they are convicted, and some rules to grant anonymity to accused persons in specific types of cases.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Law (Mr K Shanmugam)
sentences.text: If you look at examples, you have the Republic of Ireland, where accused persons charged with rape offences are granted anonymity until they are convicted, unless a judge orders otherwise.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Law (Mr K Shanmugam)
sentences.text: In Switzerland, accused persons may be granted anonymity if the court is satisfied that they could be exposed to serious danger to life and limb, or other serious prejudice.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Law (Mr K Shanmugam)
sentences.text: In New Zealand and Australia, where for jury trials, the court may prohibit the disclosure of an accused person's identity if it is satisfied that such a disclosure would create a serious risk of prejudicing a fair trial.

sections.label: Downside of public trials
sections.summary: The second approach risks irreparably damaging accused persons' reputation even if acquitted, but Singapore decided to keep publicly tried accused persons.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Law (Mr K Shanmugam)
sentences.text: The downside in this second approach is that, of course, the reputation of accused persons is often irreparably damaged by the publicity from media coverage of an on-going criminal trial, even if they are acquitted at the end of the day.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Law (Mr K Shanmugam)
sentences.text: Our approach has been to lean towards the United Kingdom example but both approaches have their merits and downsides.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Law (Mr K Shanmugam)
sentences.text: After assessments, we decided to keep our approach, which means that in general, accused persons are publicly tried and the verdict is publicly announced.

sections.label: Reviewing while maintaining status quo
sections.summary: The merits of shifting to some version of the first approach are seen, and this will be reviewed while maintaining the status quo.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Law (Mr K Shanmugam)
sentences.text: We can also see the merits of shifting to some version of the first approach.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Law (Mr K Shanmugam)
sentences.text: So, we will keep reviewing this while we are maintaining the status quo.
